utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see we have a second usher as well. I apologise, Mr. Usher. The Chamber was informed about disclosure to Ms. Loukas of Article 68 material on an empty CD. Apart from that, it sounds rather cynical to send an empty CD and say that that's the exculpatory material, if it was exculpatory material, but the Chamber is mainly interested in how to resolve the matter rather than to make a detailed investigation on how it all happened. I take it that the parties -- it was not -- there was no intent involved?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, I don't put forward that there was any intent. There is often these issues with electronic matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, you were on your feet. Would you like to add something? We are not that much interested in how it went wrong. We take it that everyone does his utmost best not to deliver any empty CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, if I can just clarify very quickly. I was informed of the position just about one minute prior to the beginning of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So was I. So let's try to see what would be needed to resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have a suggestion, Your Honour. I have hard copies in my office of the material. I can, to avoid any printing delays, et cetera, I suggest that I give that to Ms. Loukas now. I previously provided a summary of the main -- the substance of the Rule 68 within this material to Ms. Loukas, so she is aware of basically what the Rule 68 issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the material in English or...

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It is in English and B/C/S with translations in both directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's accessible for Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate, Your Honour, that Mr. Gaynor has in fact prepared a very helpful summary of the relevant material that I have received. It's just this morning I asked my case manager to actually print out the Rule 68 material, and my case manager informed me that the CD was empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood that had happened. Ms. Loukas, I do understand you get now a hard copy of the material.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Which is very helpful, Your Honour, and I'm much obliged to Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and together with the summary. We will hear from you what would be needed -- of course we have got no idea on whether this Rule 68 material would ask for any further research or investigation. I take it, Mr. Gaynor, that the material was not available to the OTP at an earlier stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I can't make that assurance, Your Honour. This material is disclosed out of an abundance of caution. I can assure you that it is overwhelmingly inculpatory. It only goes to the background of the witness. I can -- Ms. Loukas is aware of the specific issues which she might wish to cross-examine the witness on. She might not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will hear about if any further procedural decisions should be taken on the basis of this unlucky incident. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 11.00. And we could then, I take it, start in closed session again? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, the Chamber was informed that you'd like to address the Chamber. This effectively is the last day of this week for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Krajisnik case. We would very much like to see whether we can finish with the present witness. So if you could please keep it as brief as possible and consider how urgent the matter is you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the reason I come is precisely because it is the last day, and Your Honour, I have confirmed and discussed with my colleagues that there appears to be no serious difficulty about finishing the witness today. However, of course I will be as succinct as I always am, Your Honour. Your Honour -- and however Mr. Harmon wishes to take that. Your Honour, the first point is this: I've come down in the light to some extent of the exchanges in court yesterday. I, of course, have read the transcript and I see what Mr. Krajisnik had to say, so I came down specifically to see Mr. Krajisnik and to have a word with him. So that, Your Honour, is dealt with in this way, that I'll be seeing Mr. Krajisnik between now and when the Court resumes and we will consider those issues in appropriate depth. Your Honour, the second point is this: I do know that this is a matter not directly within the Trial Chamber's jurisdiction but I also know that occasionally the Trial Chamber is able to assist. Mr. Krajisnik's elder son is coming to see him and taking advantage of this short break. He hasn't seen his -- this particular son for four or five months. He's arriving today. At the moment, the only time that his son can -- who is 25 years old, the only time that he can be fitted in is Sunday morning, and then he's got to leave to go back. Your Honour, if there is any way that Mr. Krajisnik is able to see more of his son, and his son of him of course for that matter, over the next two or three days, and if there is any way that any assistance can be given. I will speak to Mr. McFadden I've only just found out about this problem. I will speak to Mr. McFadden myself to see what we can do, but any help would be very much appreciated, Your Honour. But we do understand the jurisdictional issues, but Your Honour will see how important this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar has overheard your observations, Mr. Stewart. I will ask her to see what can be done and if there is any problem to address me so that I can see whether I could assist in achieving any solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We are very grateful for that, Your Honour. And the third point is only this Your Honour, since there is a break coming up, Your Honour, I did -- well, put some and in the end a very specific question and invitation to the Trial Chamber on Wednesday, the 27th of April at close of play, and the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're talking about the scheduling order and the three weeks of recess and how to spend that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And treating the Defence team as human beings and not machines. Your Honour will recall that particular passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we would be very grateful to receive a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'll receive that response. We worked on that, if it would not have been that some other urgent matters kept me during these breaks busy, it might even have been the case that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I understand we all have urgent matters on our plate quite frequently. So I'm obliged, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not today, then at least at the beginning of next week, you would get an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. If Mr. Harmon would check his stopwatch, I think I managed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we could return into closed session. With two ushers that should be possible. And at the same time, once the curtains are down and once we are in closed session, the witness can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is coming in, I wanted to clarify for the record. Your Honour asked me to check two points on the transcript. I will do that. I won't make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I suggest that I make the clarification on the next sitting date to make sure it's absolutely right. I don't want to take the time right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, the Defence was due to give their position in respect of the Brcko dossier by last Monday. Mr. Stewart then said he was not ready yet. I asked him whether he could indicate how much more time he would need by this week. Well, this is the end of the week, as far as this Chamber is concerned. Do we know anything about it? If you do not know, there should not be a major problem. It could then perhaps be -- the Chamber could be informed through the Legal Officers by e-mail with a copy to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I can indicate that Mr. Stewart and I had discussions in relation to the dossier, and also not just the dossier for that particular municipality but in the sense of it being a template for the other municipalities, and those discussions have not been finalised because we have some suggestions of our own in relation to the -- the dossier concept for each particular municipality, and I think that Your Honour's suggestion in relation to forwarding the response by e-mail perhaps later in the week is the most efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I said later this day, because I think it was Mr. Stewart indicated that it would be by Wednesday. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would please inform the Chamber as soon as possible when you expect to give the Defence position in relation to the Brcko dossier.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other procedural issue to be raised by the parties at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Not as far as the Defence is concerned at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Nor for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn to the 17th of May in this courtroom at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th of May, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
